observed_vs_expected: The expectation of a rising best_target_score upon successful hypothesis validation is violated. The metric initially improved from 0.9872 (round 1) to 0.9934 (round 2), but then collapsed sharply to 0.9074 in the current observation. Furthermore, the expectation that tightest_margin would remain stable or improve is breached; it dropped to 0.3977, falling below the 0.5 stability threshold entirely.
deviation_mechanism: Optical path length mismatch caused by optimizer-driven layer thickness runaway. 1550 nm TMM cavity/resonator designs require precise quarter/half-wave layer thicknesses, typically clustering between 50 nm and 130 nm for common semiconductor/dielectric refractive indices. In the latest candidate evaluation, numerous layers expanded well beyond this physical optimum (exceeding 200–380 nm). These exaggerated thicknesses multiply the accumulated phase shift, detuning the cavity resonance far from the 1550 nm window and destroying the constructive interference needed for high target scoring and stopband suppression.
continue_rationale: The route has executed 3 rounds and previously achieved highly favorable scores of 0.9872 and 0.9934, demonstrating the design space is physically executable. The recent degradation to 0.9074 is explicitly tied to a localized optimizer excursion into non-resonant, overly thick parameter regions rather than a hard physical infeasibility. Because the architecture successfully recovered high performance when parameters remained moderate in earlier rounds, steering the search back into the proven operational window should yield continued gains. Halting now would prematurely discard a viable axis after a single corrective excursion.
insight_for_next: Initialize the next round using the verified high-performing profile from round 2 and impose a hard thickness ceiling of 180 nm across all layers. Apply a reduced learning rate (halved step size) for the first 10 iterations to dampen oscillatory overshoot, and add a soft quadratic penalty on deviations from 100 nm baseline thickness to anchor the solver to the known resonant basin.
insight_grounding: The performance collapse correlates directly with thickness divergence in the most recent candidate entry (fourth sublist): layer 19 expanded to 383.68 nm, layer 9 to 381.23 nm, layer 4 to 344.04 nm, and layer 23 to 368.90 nm. Compared to the tightly bounded ~100 nm profiles in round 1, these values represent 3×–3.8× excess optical path length, confirming that parameter-space drift caused the observed score drop from 0.9934 (round 2) to 0.9074 (current). Constraining to ≤180 nm directly mirrors the validated successful range that produced the 0.9934 peak.
